description: Debounced server-side validation per column in the Svelte 5 data grid: SKU uniqueness, a GTIN-13 checksum and price against the category median, checked by a mock server with latency. Each cell shows one of three states, validating with a spinner, valid with a green tick, or invalid with the reason, rendered by a cell snippet. The edit is stored immediately and the check runs in the background; a rejection marks the cell without rolling the value back.

faq.question: How is the async check triggered?
faq.answer: onCellValueChange records the edit, debounces per cell and then calls the validator for that column. The cell snippet reads the pending, valid or invalid state from a map keyed by row and column.

faq.question: Why not block the edit until the server answers?
faq.answer: Latency would make typing feel broken. Storing the value first keeps the grid responsive; the cell just shows a spinner and then a tick or the rejection reason.

faq.question: Can I validate against other rows?
faq.answer: Yes. The mock server validators receive the current row id and scan the other rows, so a duplicate SKU or barcode is rejected with the id of the row that already uses it. A real backend would run the same query against its table.
